title: KPI Trajectory Garden and Launch Flagging Protocol
summary: A lightweight, metaphor-driven tracker that treats KPIs like garden beds: we monitor growth, anticipate droughts (resource/latency shortages), and raise flags when thresholds indicate pruning or surge. Includes a minute-level staffing surge recipe, an automated flagging protocol with three escalation tiers, and acceptance criteria for go/no-go decisions.

readiness_checklist:
1) Alerts wired into #launch-ops Slack channel (owner: Ethan Ross)
2) Canary traffic route configured with 5% initial split and auto-step to 20% after 6h if no amber flags (owner: Lina Gomez)
3) Dedicated burst pool validated and capacity tested at 1.5x expected peak (owner: Platform Eng)
4) Telemetry retention for launch day extended to 72h, indices warmed (owner: Observability)
5) Incident runbook stubbed with 6 escalation contacts and clear rollback threshold (owner: SRE)
6) Cost burn monitor with finance alert at 20% over projected (owner: Finance)
7) Customer success pager for enterprise customers in pilot (owner: CS)
8) Final QA eval against core prompt set with pass rate >= 98% (owner: Applied-ML)
sprint_board:
This doc pairs with a sprint board for the 10-day launch window. Example cards:
- 'Canary routing policy: implement auto-step' | owner: Lina Gomez | estimate: 2d | status: in_progress
- 'Scale burst pool to 1.5x' | owner: Platform Eng | estimate: 1d | status: todo
- 'Run latency soak test (6h) on dedicated' | owner: Infra-API | estimate: 1d | status: todo
- 'Finalize rollback image & tag' | owner: Release Eng | estimate: 0.5d | status: in_review
Board rules: prioritize amber->green fixes before increasing traffic; any red flag triggers immediate rollback plan meeting and freeze on new feature merges.
flagging_protocol:
Tier 1 (Amber): automated alert to owners and #launch-ops; if unresolved in 30 minutes, escalate to Tier 2.
Tier 2 (Red): page on-call SRE and product-ops lead; pause traffic ramp, start containment playbook (15 min SLA to acknowledge).
Tier 3 (Critical): initiate rollback to last healthy model/deployment; notify execs and customer success; spin up postmortem channel.
Flag metadata: each flag must include timestamp, metric snapshot, recent deploy hash, and active remediation steps (text entry).
staffing_surge_recipe: Baseline rota: 8 engineers on launch-day coverage across infra, serving, SRE, applied-ml, and product-ops. Surge formula: for each 25% traffic multiplier above forecast, add +3 engineers (infra/serving) and +1 SRE on overlapping 6-hour shifts. Rapid contact list preloaded with phone numbers and backup coverage. Cross-training notes: at least 2 infra engineers know rollback image process and 1 SRE can run model hot-swap.
contingency_plans:
- Cost shock: enable 'cost-saver' routing that routes to quantized model variant and reduces max_tokens by 20%.
- Latency spike: divert 10% of traffic to cached /recommendation endpoints; temporarily increase instance size for hot shards.
- Quality regression: automatic partial rollback of model weights + freeze on new vanilla prompts; enable human-in-loop routing for enterprise accounts.
- Infra capacity loss region: failover to secondary region with degraded latency SLO and customer notice template ready.
acceptance_criteria_for_go:
1) No red flags in the preceding 6h of canary at 20% traffic.
2) Error rate <= 1.25% and P95 latency <= 160ms for serving endpoints under canary.
3) Cost projection for 24h <= 1.2x budgeted line.
4) On-call and surge roster staffed and acknowledged.
5) QA pass >= 98% on production prompt set.
6) Executives and CS notified; beta customers on standby for manual feedback.
open_questions_and_risks:
- Is the burst pool cost allocation acceptable to finance for a 72h sustained surge?
- Are enterprise customers ok with human-in-loop fallback for first 48h?
- Risk: quantized variant yields 0.7 BLEU-style drop on some evals; acceptable threshold needs signoff.
- Unknown: third-party KMS rotation schedule might conflict with private deploy key windows.

notes: Metaphor notes: 'garden' framing meant to help PMs think of KPIs as cultivatable—some need watering (capacity), some need pruning (feature throttles). Use the flagging protocol as the 'pest control' checklist. Keep the document short and operational; link to deeper runbooks for playbook steps.
